title: Cardiff seal opening Welsh derby win over Scarlets
description: Cardiff triumph in the first United Rugby Championship (URC) Welsh derby of the season by beating Scarlets in Llanelli.
fullText:
Tries: Roberts, Murray Cons: Anscombe Pens: Hawkins

Tries: D Thomas, Basham, E Lloyd Cons: Sheedy 2, Evans

Cardiff triumphed in the first United Rugby Championship (URC) Welsh derby of the season by beating Scarlets in Llanelli.

Tries from flanker Dan Thomas, player-of-the-match Taine Basham and replacement hooker Evan Lloyd helped seal the victory, with all three tries coming from effective attacking driving line-outs.

Scarlets scored first-half tries through centre Joe Roberts and full-back Blair Murray but could only manage a second-half penalty from Joe Hawkins.

Wales centre Eddie James starred for Scarlets, but he could not inspire a home victory.

It was a match played in front of a crowd of 7,073 after kicking off at the unfriendly time of quarter to eight on a Saturday evening.

Cardiff, who finished sixth last season and were the only Welsh team to reach the play-offs, were without injured Wales wing Josh Adams but gave debuts to summer signings former Australia prop Scott Sio and Namibia centre Le Roux Malan.

Scarlets, who were 14th in the 2025-26 campaign with only Dragons and Zebre below them, were missing injured number eights Fletcher Anderson and Taine Plumtree, and Wales fly-half Sam Costelow.

Wales props Corey Domachowski and Kemsley Mathias were also absent, as the hosts were led out by vice-captain Ryan Elias, who was making his 200th appearance.

It was the hosts who drew first blood with a superb break from scrum-half Dane Blacker and a neat offload from flanker Sam Lousi releasing Roberts.

Cardiff struck back with a more methodical try as flanker Thomas was driven over from an effective maul.

Scarlets again demonstrated why they looked more dangerous in possession during the first half when Murray scored a fine individual try after being expertly put through a gap by centre James, who showed the deft side in his armoury alongside the power game.

James has been employed as an outside centre by national head coach Steve Tandy but proved against Cardiff why he is a more natural inside centre with his powerful ball-carrying display.

Cardiff defence coach Gethin Jenkins would have been unimpressed by the effortless manner in which Murray glided through the visitors' defence.

Cardiff did not panic, though, and Basham powered over as the visitors led 14-12 at half-time.

In the early second-half exchanges, Murray again showed his threat as a runner, while fly-half Callum Sheedy almost created a chance for Cardiff by cheekily heading the ball after following up his kick.

Sheedy's opposite number Gareth Anscombe had made his competitive debut before he was replaced early in the second half by Joe Hawkins, who made an immediate impression by slotting over a penalty for Scarlets to regain the lead.

Another Wales fly-half, Jarrod Evans, who returned to Cardiff from Harlequins, was introduced among a raft of replacements that included Wales flanker James Botham with the bench proving crucial in the second-half success.

After a lovely sunny day in Llanelli, both sides were treated to driving rain before Scarlets wing Ellis Mee lifted the home crowd by forcing a penalty with an effective tackle and jackal.

Murray's pinpoint kick almost set up an encouraging attacking platform for Scarlets but was deemed to have gone out on the full after hitting the touchline, with referee Adam Jones consulting the television match official (TMO).

This proved a pivotal moment because Cardiff were handed an offensive position and made no mistake with replacement hooker Lloyd diving over.

Evans converted before missing a long-range penalty that would have taken Cardiff two scores clear.

Another James burst gave Scarlets hope before an important turnover from Lloyd stopped the home attack and halted any hopes of a dramatic home revival.

title: Wakefield shock Wigan to reach first Grand Final
description: Wakefield Trinity produce a sensational upset to reach their first ever Super League Grand Final and end Wigan Warriors' hopes of a treble in 2026.
fullText:
Betfred Super League play-off semi-final

Tries: Johnstone 2, Sinfield, Hall, Rodwell Goals: Jowitt 6 Drop-goal: Lino

Wakefield Trinity produced a sensational upset to reach their first ever Super League Grand Final and end Wigan Warriors' hopes of a treble in 2026.

Having led 8-6 at the end of a tight first period, the visitors took full advantage of Adam Keighran's second-half yellow card, with Tom Johnstone, Jack Sinfield and Corey Hall all crossing while the Wigan centre was in the sin-bin.

England winger Johnstone had earlier replied to Brad O'Neill's opener for the Warriors and Ky Rodwell added Wakefield's fifth try as Trinity registered 33 unanswered points to book their spot at Old Trafford.

A Championship side as recently as 2024, Wakefield have made huge progress in recent seasons under ambitious owner Matt Ellis and experienced head coach Daryl Powell - and they are now just one win away from becoming Super League champions.

They will face Warrington Wolves in the title decider on Saturday, 3 October.

Wigan went into the play-off semi-final on a 16-game winning run and with two trophies - the Challenge Cup and the League Leaders' Shield - already secured.

However, their hopes of getting to a fourth consecutive Grand Final were crushed on home soil by an outstanding Wakefield display.

'Pipe dream' to reality? Wakefield reach Grand Final

Warrington edge past Leeds to reach Grand Final

Wigan's only points came while Wakefield forward Jezz Tevaga was in the sin-bin for a trip on Liam Marshall, but it was Keighran's yellow card for a late tackle on Isaiah Vagana that proved to be the pivotal moment.

Wakefield's lead stretched from two points to 18 during Keighran's spell off the field, much to the delight of the away supporters stationed behind the end they were attacking.

Mason Lino's drop-goal and Max Jowitt's second penalty of the match added further gloss to the scoreline, and owner Ellis joined the celebrations on the field at full-time.

Only five clubs have won Grand Finals since the first was staged in 1998; Wigan, St Helens, Bradford Bulls, Leeds Rhinos and Hull KR.

Wakefield's win guarantees there will be a sixth name on the trophy and a new champion for the second successive year, following Rovers' victory in 2025.

Warrington have lost all four previous Grand Finals in which they have appeared, the most recent of them in 2018.

Powell, who was in charge of Castleford Tigers when they lost the Grand Final in 2017, is sure to be a central figure in the build-up, given his unspectacular season-and-a-half spell in charge of the Wolves which ended midway through the 2023 campaign.

Meanwhile, try-scoring half-back Sinfield is set to play in a Grand Final 11 years after his father, Sir Kevin Sinfield, made the last of his eight Grand Final appearances.

Sir Kevin won seven titles with Leeds Rhinos and he is scheduled to deliver the match ball before next Saturday's game to round off his latest fundraising effort for motor neurone disease (MND) charities.

"Hopefully he'll be there!" Jack Sinfield told BBC Two. "He's not here tonight because he's starting in the morning, but I'm sure he'll be watching and I can't wait to see him next week.

"I've been there [to Grand Finals] a fair few times watching so it will be nice to do it the other way round and he can hopefully watch me win one."

title: Man City chairman confident club will prove innocence
description: Manchester City chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak says he is still confident of proving the club's innocence after they were found guilty of breaking Premier League financial rules.
fullText:
Manchester City chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak says he is still confident of proving the club's innocence after they were found guilty of breaking the Premier League's financial rules.

City were accused of a wide range of rule breaches, centring around claims they inflated sponsorship revenue from connected companies and made other "off the books" payments to circumvent financial regulations.

On Friday, it was announced City had been found guilty of the vast majority of the 115 charges brought against them and Al Mubarak has responded with a letter to fans on the club's website.

"Following Friday's media reporting, many of you will have spent your evening answering questions and responding to messages from friends, family and colleagues. So have I," Al Mubarak said.

"Here's what I said to my family: The Premier League process still has a long way to run, and our confidence and intent in proving the club's innocence is just as strong as when this began.

"There are so many things that I would like to be able to share with you to help you understand why we feel so confident in our position.

"But the strict confidentiality of the legal process and our determination to respect it means I cannot do that at the moment. Even this letter underwent several legal checks to make sure it complies."

Premier League clubs are seeking legal advice about compensation relating to the charges, while BBC Sport has been told City will appeal.

Sanctions on the club are yet to be announced, but repercussions could include a points deduction, expulsion from the Premier League or a huge fine.

Al Mubarak, who was appointed as City's chairman after their 2008 takeover, also said his club was being "undermined".

"While some people have been quick to reach their own conclusions, and there is so much noise swirling around us, nothing has changed. We have faced challenges together before and have prevailed," he added.

"There remain many who want to undermine the momentum of our club. We will not give them that opportunity."

Man City and the 115 charges - key questions answered

Man City fans face up to reality of guilty verdict

Everton told to pay Burnley £35m over PSR breach

Manchester City vs The Premier League

Meanwhile, Christian Purslow, a former Liverpool managing director and Aston Villa chief executive, who also held a senior role at Chelsea, said the City case could begin a chain of events that would be "appalling for the game".

Speaking on Radio 4's Today programme, Purslow appeared alongside football law expert Paul Gilroy KC, who described the case as a "seismic moment for world football".

Purslow said: "It's a sort of 'where does this end?' because if you look at every single season - the nine seasons which we now know Manchester City breached rules - then all of their 19 Premier League rivals in that season, to differing extents, suffered easy-to-compute loss. Whether it was a place in the Premier League - every place was worth £3m.

"Teams that came fifth who didn't make the Champions League maybe lost tens of millions of pounds - and of course teams that were relegated. Let's say the team that finished 18th would've finished 17th if Manchester City weren't there. And they, of course, suffered huge loss.

"If you add all those claims up, over nine years, and that's just in the Premier League, you can see that the potential here for this to spiral out of control is huge."

Gilroy added that, so far, four clubs have put in protective claims "reserving the right to claim compensation if City are found guilty".

The news, broken by the Athletic,, external came 1,327 days after City were charged by the Premier League in February 2023 following a four-year investigation, and 22 months after a hearing by an independent commission concluded.

No official announcement has been made by the Premier League, which has declined to comment.

Manchester City declined to comment on whether they had been found guilty, instead providing a statement which read: "Premier League process remains ongoing with significant elements to be completed, and subject to strict confidentiality.

"The club has diligently respected due process for eight years on the basis that the Premier League board and executive would behave as an independent, impartial and fair-minded regulator, free from partisan influence."

Culture Secretary Lisa Nandy has urged the Premier League to come to a quick resolution.

She told BBC Radio 5 Live: "I think most football fans will be feeling that this is not a good moment for football as a whole and I think Manchester City fans will be feeling very, very anxious about what happens next.

"It's very unsettling for football fans and I hope that it can be resolved as swiftly as possible.

"I will obviously look very closely as what comes out of this but we can't apply those rules for the Premier League. They have got to do it themselves and are going to have to resolve this as swiftly as possible - not just for the sake of Manchester City but for the sake of football."

City won eight trophies in the period covered by the case, including three Premier League titles, three EFL Cups, one Community Shield and one FA Cup.

The charges cover the managerial tenures of Roberto Mancini and Manuel Pellegrini, and the first two years under Pep Guardiola, who left the club at the end of last season after 10 years in charge.

David Bernstein, who was Manchester City chairman from 1998-2003, told Times Radio he felt "absolutely awful" on hearing the news of City being found guilty - but admitted any punishment would have to be "more drastic" than a fine.

"To see all this tarnished in this way is very sad," he said.

"I feel particularly bad for the wonderful supporters of the club who've stayed with the club through thick and thin.

"This whole process has taken too long already. So the appeal process now has to be done quickly because you've got the club playing with this cloud over its head and it's just not viable.

"The appeal process cannot go on for year after year, I think that would be a disaster, not just for this particular case but for English football generally. The timing is crucial."

He continued: "I can't give a view on the punishment. If they are found, after the appeal, guilty of 115 charges, my beloved club is going to face a very severe penalty.

"All I would say is that money is not sufficient, it would have to be something, unfortunately, more drastic than that."

Meanwhile, singer-songwriter Noel Gallagher says he is "shocked" at the news and it is "quite sad" for players and fans.

"A little surprised when I heard it on the radio. Surprised because the club have assured us all along that they vehemently denied any of these charges," the Oasis star and City fan said on the Let Me Talk podcast.

"So it was a bit of a shock to find out that we've been found guilty. But really overall just quite sad really. Sad for the fans and for the players."

title: Who made an uncharacteristic error? England player ratings v Spain
description: England were beaten 3-2 in an entertaining game by world champions Spain in the Nations League - here's how BBC Sport rated the Three Lions' players.
fullText:
England were beaten 3-2 in an entertaining game by world champions Spain in the Nations League - the Three Lions' first match since this summer's World Cup.

Lamine Yamal gave Spain the lead before goals from Anthony Gordon and Harry Kane put England ahead.

Kane then missed a penalty before Alex Baena curled in to level the score, with Mikel Oyarzabal scoring the winner.

Here's how we rated England's players - and you can have your say in the comments at the bottom.

James Trafford: Showed early on his ability to play with the ball at his feet but conceded after just two minutes when Guehi gifted the ball to Lamine Yamal. An important save stopped Torres making it 2-0 in the first half. 6

Jarell Quansah: Continued at right-back after showing what he could do in the position at the World Cup. A physically dominant performance and had a chance to score but headed over. 6

Ezri Konsa: Some shaky moments for Konsa and England's back four but the centre-back regrouped and got better as the game went on. 6

Nico O'Reilly: Put in the cross for Kane's goal as England took the lead in the first half. Did a good job of trying to deal with Lamine Yamal. However he gave the ball away for Spain's second goal. 6

Elliot Anderson: Nearly punished for giving the ball away in a dangerous position in the first half but Ferran Torres rolled his shot wide. Anderson and midfield partner Lewis-Skelly took some time to settle in what was a tough night in the middle of the pitch against a Spain side who moved the ball so well. 6

Myles Lewis-Skelly: A first England start in centre midfield for Lewis-Skelly after shining for Arsenal. Given the tough task of trying to shut off the supply to Spain's conductor, Rodri. A solid performance. Replaced after 70 minutes. 6

Harry Kane: Started dropping deep in the first half in search of the ball after England went behind. Scored the second with a deflected header to put England in the lead but missed a penalty when they had the chance to add a third in the second half. 7

title: Internationals hold three-point lead over US
description: The Internationals team could secure a first President's Cup in 28 years on Sunday after holding off a United States fightback on day three in Medinah.
fullText:
The International team need five points on the final day to secure a first Presidents Cup in 28 years after holding off a United States fightback on day three in Medinah.

The Internationals were behind in every match at one stage but will go into Sunday's singles holding a 10-5-7.5 lead.

The hosts had the better of the morning session, winning two and tying one of the four-balls.

But the teams split the afternoon foursomes, with Canada's Corey Conners saving par at the 18th to win the final match on the course and preserve the Internationals' three-point lead.

The International team have only won the President's Cup once since its inception in 1994 and never on American soil.

"We were down in every match, and to come back and get one and a half points out of this morning, we felt that was a little victory because we were down everywhere," said team captain Geoff Ogilvy.

"This afternoon, the same thing happened. Team USA played so well all day. They played some really high-level foursomes, especially this afternoon.

"For the boys to somehow come back and pinch two points out of that and split the session was amazing."

Sunday sees 12 singles games take place, with each side needing 15.5 points to seal victory.

title: Pickford or Trafford? The battle to be England's number one is now on
description: Jordan Pickford has been England's number one for a long time. But does he now have a rival in James Trafford?
fullText:
You have to go back 10 years to find a major tournament where Jordan Pickford was not starting in goal for England.

The Everton goalkeeper has pretty much been England's number one since making his debut in 2017 - until now.

Saturday's 3-2 Nations League loss to Spain saw Leeds' James Trafford make his competitive debut for the Three Lions as manager Thomas Tuchel signalled the battle to be number one is on.

Pickford became England's highest appearance maker at World Cups, overtaking Peter Shilton when he started in England's 2026 quarter-final win over Norway.

During Gareth Southgate's tenure there was not a natural goalkeeper to rival Pickford, and that looked to continue under Tuchel as Pickford started all but one of England's World Cup qualifiers and then every game in the summer.

But it looks as though Pickford has finally got a rival in Trafford, with Tuchel saying that the pair get "two consecutive matches each" during this international break.

Trafford has impressed since making his move to Leeds for a deal worth up to £45m.

Against Spain, the 23-year-old showed his quality with the ball at his feet and made an impressive save to deny Ferran Torres in the first half.

But he was beaten three times as England lost their Nations League opener to the world champions.

"I think he deserved to get the two matches, that's why we gave him two matches," Tuchel said.

"He started the Premier League season well and gets minutes as number one at Leeds.

"Jordan [Pickford] did absolutely nothing wrong but we wanted to use this competition to see how far actually James is."

Trafford's form this season has helped Leeds to fifth in the Premier League table.

He has kept two clean sheets and now has his chance to stake his claim as England's future number one over two matches.

Trafford had only played 32 top-flight games before moving to Leeds following time at Burnley and Manchester City.

He came through City's academy and joined Burnley for an initial fee of £15m in the summer of 2023.

However, he conceded 67 goals in only 28 matches before losing his place towards the end of the 2023-24 season.

But after starring in Burnley's successful promotion in 2024-25 and the Clarets conceding just 16 goals, Trafford returned to City for £27m last summer with the hope of being Pep Guardiola's number one.

City brought in one of the best goalkeepers in the world in Gianluigi Donnarumma, just four weeks after Trafford's arrival and he became second choice.

Despite it being a frustrating campaign, Trafford did get vital experience and started both the FA Cup final and Carabao Cup final for City before his move to Leeds.

He has been part of England success too, winning the U21 European Championship in 2023 and saving a stoppage-time penalty as Lee Carsley's side beat Spain in the final.

Pickford has kept 46 clean sheets in his 91 appearances for England and has been a huge part of the Three Lions' recent success at major tournaments.

"I think Jordan Pickford will be very disappointed," former England goalkeeper Paul Robinson said on BBC Radio 5 Live.

"Putting myself in that place, he will be questioning why he is not in that place. If he is number one, then why is he not playing against the world champions?

"You wonder whether this is the next generation coming through for Thomas Tuchel."

Pickford put in an excellent performance as England beat Mexico in the World Cup to progress to the quarter-finals, but it was not the goalkeeper's best tournament.

"Jordan Pickford has never let England down," Ian Dennis said.

"You have opposition against the Czech Republic and Croatia where you could give James Trafford an opportunity then. I do find the decision quite strange.

"Pickford against the world champions - you would back him to play in this game."

Pickford is in current possession of the number one shirt and played every minute of the World Cup until he was rested for England's third-place play-off win over France, with Dean Henderson starting.

The 32-year-old, who will be 34 at Euro 2028, has 91 England caps and has saved four of the 14 penalties he has faced in major tournament shootouts.

In the Premier League Pickford's overall numbers dwarf Trafford's. Since the start of the 2024-25 season no-one has prevented more expected goals than the Everton stopper.

But there is very little between the two this campaign with Pickford preventing more goals but Trafford having a higher save percentage and better passing accuracy.

Pickford has been fantastic for England but he didn't have the best World Cup, with a couple conceded that arguably he should've saved and a few nervy moments playing out from the back. Now seems as good a time as any to try James Trafford.

James Trafford deserves to start, he's going to be England's next number one and why not start him against Spain or would you rather he only played against third-rate nations?

James Trafford deserves his shot! Jordan Pickford has been quality for 10 years! Time feels right to test who could be next. Finding the next Harry Kane is going to be the problem!

Jordan Pickford is paying the price for those mistakes creeping in during the World Cup. Could he have stopped the goals v Croatia, DR Congo and Fernandez v Argentina? Prime Pickford does. Thomas Tuchel showing his ruthless side again.

title: Fisher outpoints bloodied Pirotton on Zuffa debut
description: British heavyweight Johnny Fisher wins his first fight under the Zuffa Boxing banner with a majority points victory over Michael Pirotton at the Copper Box Arena.
fullText:
British heavyweight Johnny Fisher won his first fight under the Zuffa Boxing banner with a majority points victory over a bloodied Michael Pirotton at London's Copper Box Arena.

The 27-year-old Essex fighter was the deserved winner in a close bout, but looked laboured at times and appeared to feel the pace over 10 rounds.

Belgian Pirotton, 30, was hampered by a cut around the eye from early in the fight but battled gamely.

He was rocked in the final round as Fisher briefly threatened a stoppage, but Pirotton held on as the judges scored it 95-95, 98-92 and 96-95.

Fisher left the ring shortly after his arm was raised without doing an interview and also did not attend a post-fight interview.

It was Fisher's 15th victory in 16 professional contests on his first appearance since leaving Matchroom Boxing and joining Dana White's Zuffa promotion.

The 7,500-capacity Copper Box was some way short of full, with the upper tier closed and empty seats dotted around the arena.

But Fisher's "Bosh Army" did their best to fill the gaps with noise, giving the "Romford Bull" a raucous reception.

Alongside his social-media star father "Big John", Fisher has built a loyal following through an unusually unfiltered glimpse into family life, training camps and the pair's well-documented enthusiasm for Chinese takeaways.

Fisher started with intent, swinging heavy hooks and reddening Pirotton's eye in the opening round.

The little-known Belgian was unfazed by the home support or Fisher's pressure, but his eye was cut by the second.

"I can see, don't stop the fight," Pirotton told the referee before a doctor examined him in the fourth.

Allowed to continue, he came out firing, but Fisher responded with a flurry to head and body.

Blood stained Pirotton's white shorts, yet he rallied in the fifth - his best round - as Fisher began to look tired and static.

Among those in attendance were British fighters Derek Chisora, Conor Benn and Caroline Dubois, alongside WWE stars AJ Styles and LA Knight.

WWE is owned by American sports and entertainment group TKO, which is also behind Zuffa Boxing.

The doctor took another look at Pirotton before the seventh but allowed the bout to continue.

Neither man was offering much by the latter stages until a short right hand from Fisher staggered Pirotton in the 10th.

For a moment, a 13th stoppage victory appeared within reach, but Fisher could not find the finishing burst as Pirotton slipped to his third loss in 15 fights.

The Copper Box Arena has already become a fitting stage for the contrasting fortunes of Fisher's career. In July 2024, he overwhelmed Alen Babic in just 36 seconds, producing his most explosive victory to date.

Ten months later, in the same ring, he was comprehensively stopped in five rounds by Doncaster's Dave Allen.

Keen to put that behind him, Fisher got the victory he needed on Saturday - if not quite the emphatic performance he might have wanted.

Fisher has repeatedly insisted he wants to be known as more than a popular ticket-seller with a catchy nickname and viral antics.

His profile has raced ahead of his achievements in the ring, and the two meetings with Allen offered the clearest indication yet of the gap he must close if his British-title ambitions are to become reality.

Current British heavyweight champion Richard Riakporhe has already offered Fisher a shot at the belt. The former cruiserweight world champion would represent a considerable jump in level and a far sterner examination than Pirotton.

Former world champion Deontay Wilder has also been mooted as an opponent, but a meeting with former world-title challenger Dillian Whyte appears the more realistic possibility, with Fisher saying there is a "good chance" that contest could come next.

title: Tuchel rues 'big mistakes' - did Man City charges have impact?
description: England's loss to Spain was decided by uncharacteristic mistakes, with two Man City players making errors - so did club news affect performances for country?
fullText:
It was a match full of world-class players - but England's loss to Spain was ultimately decided by uncharacteristic mistakes.

Just a day after Manchester City were found guilty of breaking Premier League financial rules, two errors by City players - Nico O'Reilly and Marc Guehi - gifted world champions Spain two goals.

And former City midfielder Rodri, who moved to Barcelona in the summer, also gave away a penalty in Spain's 3-2 win on Saturday.

Pundit Roy Keane was among those left to wonder whether news of the verdict had affected players with City ties.

Asked if it was a distraction after his side's loss at Wembley, England boss Thomas Tuchel said: "Not for me but I can imagine for the Manchester City players.

"For the players who have more time than me, for sure I can imagine they talk about it."

Speaking to ITV Sport former Manchester United captain Keane said: "In top level football you want to be focused and they certainly would have been affected.

"To see so many top-class players make so many mistakes - it has certainly affected them."

Man City and the 115 charges - key questions answered

Manchester City vs The Premier League

Three City players - Elliot Anderson, Guehi and O'Reilly - started for England, while Rodri, who spent seven years at the club, was in Spain's XI.

And three of those four players made significant errors at Wembley.

First Guehi was tackled by Lamine Yamal on the edge of his own box, allowing the Spain winger to drive towards goal and slot in his side's opener.

In the second half Rodri's late challenge on Jude Bellingham led to an England penalty, which Harry Kane struck against the crossbar after slipping.

And then O'Reilly had a pass intercepted deep in his own half which led to Alex Baena's equaliser at 2-2.

On Friday, sources told BBC Sport City had been found guilty of breaking the majority of the 115 financial rules they were accused of breaching.

After a four-year investigation, the club were accused of a wide range of rule breaches centring around claims they inflated sponsorship revenue and made other "off the books" payments to circumvent financial rules between 2009 and 2018.

Sanctions are yet to be announced, but repercussions could include a points deduction, expulsion from the Premier League or a huge fine.

BBC Sport understands Premier League clubs are seeking legal advice about potential compensation.

England captain Kane played down any links between the charges and player mistakes, telling ITV Sport after Saturday's game: "There was a discussion, but at the end of the day when we're with England we kind of put club football to one side and it was no different this week."

A few hours before kick-off at Wembley, City chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak told supporters he was still confident of proving the club's innocence and the "Premier League process still has a long way to run".

Spain captain Rodri had also stressed his belief in the club's innocence in a news conference on Friday.

"They always express the confidence that they never did something wrong and we believe in that," he said.

"Until the moment they are proved wrong, we will believe the club. They always tell us the confidence they have on the innocence."

The charges cover the managerial tenures of Roberto Mancini and Manuel Pellegrini, and the first two years under Pep Guardiola, who left the club after 10 seasons at the end of the 2025-26 campaign.

City won the Premier League and EFL Cup three times and FA Cup once between 2009 and 2018.

Guehi, Rodri and O'Reilly all made their City debuts after the period in question.

title: Vollering wins women's road race world title
description: Demi Vollering continues her remarkable season with a thrilling victory in the women's road race in Montreal.
fullText:
Demi Vollering continued her remarkable season with a thrilling victory to win the women's road race world title in Montreal.

The Dutchwoman held off a late challenge from Kasia Niewiadoma-Phinney to add another title to her collection, following wins at the Tour de France Femmes, Giro d'Italia Women and World Championships.

The 29-year-old also won a string of one-day classics in the spring, including the Tour of Flanders and Liege-Bastogne-Liege.

"I can still not believe it. I worked so hard towards this goal, and it takes guts to truly believe in it with your whole heart," she said.

Italian Elisa Longo Borghini edged out world time-trial champion Marlen Reusser to take bronze.

Great Britain's Flora Perkins was among 15 riders to crash while speeding downhill early in the race.

Defending champion Magdeleine Vallieres, Mauritius' Kimberley Le Court and Spain's Paula Blasi were also involved and eventually had to withdraw.

Vollering launched her initial attack with about 40km to go only to be reeled in by the chasing pack over the final two laps.

Poland's Niewiadoma-Phinney stayed on her wheel in the closing stages but was beaten to the line, with Vollering claiming victory in four hours 45 minutes nine seconds.

"There were so many moments I thought I went too early," Vollering said. "I didn't dare to turn around and look back because I felt like they were almost on my wheel already.

"I just dared, tried again and never gave up to the finish line."

title: England embrace the chaos - but control also needed to win big prizes
description: England embrace the chaos, but superb Spain show it will never win big prizes, says chief football writer Phil McNulty.
fullText:
Thomas Tuchel talked about England having to "embrace the chaos" as they embarked on recovery from the crushing disappointment of World Cup semi-final defeat by Argentina.

As England took those first steps on the road to rehabilitation against reigning world and European champions Spain in the Nations League at Wembley, head coach Tuchel learned the brutal lesson that chaos without control is a loser's strategy at elite level.

Spain do control, not chaos. And this is why they are serial winners and England remain a nearly team without a major men's success since the 1966 World Cup.

England delivered moments to admire in the 3-2 defeat, even embracing those chaotic spells in an enthralling encounter, but ultimately they came up short once more against this summer's World Cup winners, who are now unbeaten in 39 games.

Once Tuchel's England stopped playing themselves into trouble by mimicking Spain's passing style without having anywhere near the quality of their opponents and followed their own "DNA", to use the buzz-phrase of the moment, they actually threatened with power and pace.

Quite how England reached the 36th minute only one goal down was a mystery to everyone inside Wembley, Marc Guehi's inexplicable turn into trouble gifting Lamine Yamal an opener inside two minutes.

Ferran Torres saw a goal ruled out for offside, was denied by a fine stop by England goalkeeper James Trafford, then rolled an effort wide of the post when clean through.

England took advantage of those reprieves to somehow be ahead by the break, through star performer Anthony Gordon's composed finish and Harry Kane's deflected header.

Kane's penalty miss just after the break was a turning point, hitting the bar after slipping and touching the ball twice, before England once again paid the price for errors.

Nico O'Reilly coughed up possession in the build-up to Alex Baena's equaliser before another substitute in Mikel Oyarzabal, who scored the winner in the Euro 2024 final against England in Berlin, settled matters after 74 minutes.

If it was a bad night for Manchester City defensive duo Guehi and O'Reilly, it was not much better for Jarell Quansah, who was given the nod ahead of the recalled Trent Alexander-Arnold. He was uncertain throughout and does not look a natural right-back - perhaps because he is not a natural right-back.

Of course, it could have been different had Kane scored his penalty. He did not and it was not.

Kane said: "On another day we could have won." This was not another day and England did not win.

England's bolder approach after a shaky opening 25 minutes offered up the prospect of a landmark victory, but shambolic defending saw Guehi and O'Reilly present gifts Spain were happy to accept.

As against Argentina in the World Cup semi-final in Atlanta, England led by a Gordon goal and lost, but at least here they went down swinging and not by going into cowering retreat.

It was a small mercy appreciated by the home support, but the gulf in class when it mattered was still evident as Spain's smooth, unhurried style cut a sharp contrast to England's often frantic efforts.

Tuchel's defence looked horribly vulnerable and easy to slice through, although keeper Trafford – given two games before first-choice Jordan Pickford returns – was blameless and will have created a good impression as he tries to create greater competition in that department.

They have now shipped 13 goals in their last six matches in all competitions, after conceding only seven in their first 17 games under Tuchel.

Ironically, it was two players now plying their trade in Spain, Gordon at Barcelona and Jude Bellingham at Real Madrid, who were England's standout performers.

Gordon was in electrifying form, while Bellingham was relentless in driving England forward, even in a losing cause.

As for the chaos, Tuchel begged to differ.

He told BBC Radio 5 Live: "I'm not sure there was a lot of chaos. We had an incredible amount of high-ball recoveries in the opponent's half. I think 15 more than Spain. Overall, I think 15 in total in the first half. That only goes against a team like Spain if we play man to man, so we were very brave."

Tuchel added: "The defending and the deep block were excellent, except for the third goal where we got cut open through the middle. This normally should not happen.

"Offensively, I think we played in a clear structure. We tried to switch sides a lot. We tried to put the full-backs up to make the difference and they did. A lot of good stuff but unfortunately not the result."

On the gap between the sides, Tuchel said: "We saw no gap except for the technical execution. In the last 20 metres, they were superior than us."

Tuchel's comments are questionable here, ignoring the fact that if Spain's own technical execution was better they could easily have been four goals up before England scored, but he was correct to point out the improvement after Gordon drew them level.

England captain Kane said: "I spoke before that we reached good levels at the World Cup but didn't quite put a full 90 minutes together. It was probably similar again here. We had a couple of good moments though, that period was as good as we've played in a long, long time and that's the standard we know we can reach.

"We're playing against the world champions, the European champions, and we went toe-to-toe. On another day for sure we'd have won that game."

England certainly embrace the chaos, as Tuchel suggested, but chaos alone does not claim big prizes and never has.

At least this is a lesson Tuchel did not have to wait too long to learn after the World Cup.

title: 'Pipe dream' to reality? Wakefield reach Grand Final
description: Wakefield Trinity were playing in rugby league's second tier in 2024. Two years on, they are one win away from becoming Super League champions.
fullText:
"It's something I've dreamed about for years and it used to be a bit of a pipe dream," said Tom Johnstone, when asked about the prospect of Wakefield Trinity winning a Super League Grand Final.

That dream could become a reality for the England winger on 3 October, after Wakefield shocked treble-chasing Wigan Warriors 33-6 in Saturday's play-off semi-final to secure their place in the Old Trafford showpiece for the first time.

Wakefield, who will play Warrington Wolves in the title decider, have been a club transformed in recent seasons.

So often competing at the wrong end of the Super League table, they lost their top-flight status in 2023 - but that proved to be the beginning of the club's reinvigoration, sparked by the completion of a takeover by kitchen magnate Matt Ellis.

His financial support, along with the leadership and experience of head coach Daryl Powell, have led Wakefield up from the Championship and now to within 80 minutes of becoming Super League champions.

Johnstone, 31, began his career with Wakefield and was back for Trinity's return to the top division at the start of 2025 after a two-year spell with Catalans Dragons.

"I went to Matt's kitchen factory with my agent and we had a chat about everything they want to achieve and everything they promised to do," Johnstone, who scored two of Wakefield's five tries against Wigan, told BBC Two.

"We left and said: 'If they do any of that, it's going to be something special.' I couldn't say no."

Powell, who was appointed shortly after Wakefield had dropped into the second tier, added: "The journey's been an interesting one.

"We got relegated but it was probably good for us. It allowed us to stabilise the team, get our staff in and sign some players that got us out of the Championship.

"We started to sign high-quality players like Mike [McMeeken] and Tom, and some of the guys we signed the year before have really grown and prospered."

Wakefield shock Wigan to reach first Grand Final

Warrington edge past Leeds to reach Grand Final

Prior to the semi-final, many viewed Wakefield - who finished fourth in Super League - as second favourites against a Wigan team that had won 16 successive matches and were seeking a second domestic treble in the space of three seasons.

But Trinity responded brilliantly to falling behind early on and took full advantage of Adam Keighran's second-half yellow card, seizing control of the contest and winning it with 33 unanswered points.

Ex-England half-back Kevin Brown, working as a BBC pundit, described Wakefield's display against Wigan as "definitely their best ever performance in Super League", adding: "It's been an incredible story where we're at right now and we're going to run out of superlatives if they go and win it."

Captain McMeeken has played in three previous Grand Finals with Castleford and Catalans, while he was also part of the England side that played in a World Cup semi-final on home soil in 2022 - but the significance of Saturday's achievement was not lost on him, either.

"To take in an experience like this is up there as one of the best moments of my career so far," he said.

At Old Trafford, Powell will come up against the club he coached for a season and a half before his exit midway through the 2023 campaign.

He said: "It's not about me or my journey, it's about the players and how they're writing different scripts every time we take the field."

Whoever is victorious will be a first-time Super League champion and Powell added: "It'll be awesome for the game. I think it's awesome that we're there in particular, Warrington have been there before.

"For us, it's about not getting too ahead of ourselves, playing the game as it is like we did tonight, and if we do that, we've got a great chance."

title: Analysis: Wayshawn Parker’s huge day helps Utah overcome poor 3rd quarter in win at Iowa State
description: Thanks to one of the best performances of Wayshawn Parker’s career, the Utes escaped Jack Trice Stadium with a 31-17 victory to open Big 12 play.
fullText:
AMES, Iowa — Thanks to one of the best performances of Wayshawn Parker's career, the No. 15 Utah Utes escaped Jack Trice Stadium with a 31-17 victory over the Iowa State Cyclones Saturday to open Big 12 play and improve to 4-0 on the season.

Parker ran for 174 yards and two touchdowns on 18 carries and added 65 receiving yards and a touchdown to contribute a total of 239 all-purpose yards in the Utes' win.

It was clear from the opening snap that it was going to be Parker's day. With the white-clad fans at the mostly-full stadium in a frenzy as Utah took the field for the first possession of the game, it was Parker, not quarterback Devon Dampier, who took the snap.

Parker turned toward Dampier, then darted toward the middle of the field, squeezing between a couple of Iowa State defensive linemen before beating safety Duhron Goodman in a footrace for a 54-yard touchdown that put Utah up 7-0 fewer than 20 seconds into the game and quieted a raucous crowd.

"That was huge. They wanted to give us the ball first. We take that personal anytime a team wants to give us the ball first. For Way to break that, for the (offensive) line to make that hole for him, huge excitement," Dampier said.

"Definitely silenced the crowd a little bit. Just kind of felt like we had momentum during that time and we just kept using it, kept building off of it."

Parker's 54-yard opening salvo was just a taste of his performance in the victory. After a quiet game last week against Utah State with just 30 rushing yards, Parker proved why he's one of the best running backs in the Big 12 with a game that saved a dreadful third-quarter performance by the Utes on a dreary day in Ames.

"Really proud of Wayshawn Parker," Utah coach Morgan Scalley said. "I mean, this is a guy that all he does is everything that you ask. You watch this kid when he doesn't have the ball and he goes and he runs and blocks and he picks up his teammates and he celebrates with his teammates.

"He deserves everything good that comes his way. Really proud of him."

Whether Parker was running the ball or catching it, it was tough for Iowa State's defense to bring down the 205-pound running back, especially in the first half. Of his 65 receiving yards, 62 came after the catch, and an astounding 137 of his 174 rushing yards came after contact.

On one play in the first half, Parker made five Iowa State defenders miss.

Parker's biggest offseason improvement was in the receiving game, where he's become a reliable option for Dampier. After four games with a total of 154 receiving yards, Parker is already close to surpassing his 2025 13-game total of 185.

But Parker didn't just shine on his touchdown runs and catches Saturday. He was counted on in a number of short yardage situations, including a fourth and 1, and came through time and time again, sucking the energy out of the stadium throughout the first half.

Then when the Utes absolutely needed a touchdown to put the game to bed late in the fourth quarter, they went back to Parker, who only got two carries in a third quarter wherein Utah didn't possess the ball much.

With the Utes up just seven points with 7:26 left after forcing a three-and-out on their best defensive stand of the game, offensive coordinator Kevin McGiven made sure to give Parker the rock on the game-deciding drive.

Parker carried the ball three consecutive times to start the drive and got the Utes deep into Iowa State territory, then finished off the possession with a 13-yard touchdown reception from Dampier on third and 1.

"Just knowing coach McGiven, he already told me that he was going to put the ball in my hands. Going out there and knowing that I got the team on my back, it just made it much easier," Parker said.

"The O line, you got to get props to the O line first. They made some gaps for me to go through. Got to give props to Dev because he's a dual threat. They got to worry about him, too. Going on that field, I already knew it was going to work and what was going to happen."

That touchdown essentially polished off a game that got dicey in the second half for the Utes.

It was certainly a tale of two halves for Utah. The Utes dominated the first two quarters, shutting down the Iowa State rushing attack.

Without being able to rely on the rushing game that got them out to a surprising start this season, the Cyclones managed just 41 rushing yards in the first half. Lead running back Aiden Flora was stymied by Utah's defensive front, rushing for only 14 yards in the first two quarters.

The Utes went into the locker room up 24-3 after outgaining the Cyclones 272-139 behind Parker's monster half and an efficient 12 for 15 passing performance by Dampier.

While McGiven's offense showed a lot of trickery in its first three games, it was encouraging that Utah didn't need to rely on that to move the ball and score touchdowns.

In fact, the first half was as "vanilla" of an offense as we've seen all season from the Utes, though Scalley considers what many people call "trick plays" just part of the normal offense.

"It's just game plan by game plan, what are their strengths? How are we going to expose that or take advantage of that? And our offensive staff did a really nice job of making sure based on the looks they were giving us, that determined what we were going to try and do to them," Scalley said.

But the second half looked like a completely different Utah team.

Iowa State dominated the third-quarter time of possession 10:01 to 4:53 as it found much more success offensively, moving the ball with ease to start the second half.

The Cyclones only faced two third downs on the opening 12-play, 82-yard drive that ended with a Jalyen Raynor keeper that fooled everyone on Utah's defense.

Iowa State then closed the gap to seven points to open the fourth quarter with another lengthy drive. Raynor converted a third and 7 on a scramble, and even when the Utes forced the Cyclones into a fourth and 12, the home team still converted with a pass from Raynor to Utahn Dominic Overby that moved the chains after a lengthy review.

On the next play, Raynor found a wide-open Overby again to pull the Cyclones within 24-17.

"What did they do differently offensively? Well, a little bit 

"Obviously they were trying to create mismatches, putting a wide receiver in the backfield, shifting them out on air, but probably a little bit 

After the Utes did nothing with their next possession, it was on the defense to come up with a big stop in the fourth quarter after struggling in the third.

"I got to be better decision making. A lot of that falls on me, where I'm getting the ball out, where I'm looking on the field. A lot of those were in passing downs, so I just got to be more efficient on my part," Dampier said of the offense's third-quarter performance.

"But we learn from those. We got things to learn from from this game and promise we'll come back stronger."

Facing adversity for the first time this season, Utah showed impressive resolve in digging deep and forcing a three-and-out that was capped off by an Elijah Elliss sack.

"You look at near the end when we started to bring six, put more heat on the quarterback, that's when I thought we had some success, so tried to just counter that with bringing the heat," Scalley said.

After the Iowa State punt, Parker found paydirt on the ensuing series to make sure the Utes remained undefeated.

title: Steve Sarkisian blames "society" for Colin Simmons's bizarre unsportsmanlike conduct foul
description: To cap a week in which the NFL went overboard with fines, Texas defensive end Colin Simmons did something that possibly would have gotten him banned for life by 345 Park Avenue.
fullText:
To cap a week in which the NFL went overboard with fines, Texas defensive end Colin Simmons did something that possibly would have gotten him banned for life by 345 Park Avenue.

After one of his Longhorn record-tying five sacks against Tennessee, Simmons celebrated by pretending to urinate on the field.

He seemed surprised when the officials penalized the move, with the eventual explanation being that Simmons was "simulating using the restroom."

Coach Steve Sarkisian addressed the situation following the 20-17 win.

"We took him out," Sarkisian said, via Tyler Lauletta of Awful Announcing, regarding the fact that Simmons, well, took it out. "We addressed it, and put him back in. I'm not gonna give the guy the death penalty over an unsportsmanlike conduct penalty. We've got to fix it though. That can't continue as we move forward."

That part is reasonable and appropriate. Then, things got a little screwy from Sarkisian.

"Unfortunately, in our society right now, we live in the 'look at me' society," Sarkisian said. "All of you guys have your Twitter accounts, and as fast as you can type something because you want everyone to look at your account, and you get clicks. Well, that's the world that we live in. So we've got to get to —it's about the team and focus on the team, and not so much 'look at me.' So we'll try to improve upon that, but five sacks was pretty cool today too."

Steve, don't simulate using the restroom on our leg and tell us it's raining. Society didn't lead Simmons to do something we've never seen a player do, because 99.999999 percent of all players know not to do it.

Still, we'd love to hear how Sarkisian would explain a similarly perverse celebration that was not penalized. Almost as much as we'd love to hear the explanation of the foul.

Texas star defensive end Colin Simmons turned heads against Tennessee on Saturday, putting together a historic performance that was tempered by an unsportsmanlike conduct penalty stemming from an inappropriate sack celebration. The No. 1 Longhorns escaped Knoxville with a 20-17 win over the No. 14 Volunteers, improving to 4-0.

Simmons finished with eight tackles, including six solo stops, five sacks, a forced fumble, 10 total pressures and two quarterback hits. His five sacks tied the Texas single-game program record and marked the most sacks by an SEC player since at least 2000, according to ESPN. He also became the first FBS player in 20 seasons to record five sacks against a ranked opponent, per ESPN Insights.

The incident came in the second quarter after Simmons dropped Tennessee true freshman quarterback Faizon Brandon for a 16-yard loss. Following the sack, Simmons mimicked urinating on the field, prompting officials to call him for unsportsmanlike conduct for "simulating using the restroom."

Because the play occurred on third-and-13, the 15-yard penalty resulted in an automatic first down for the Volunteers instead of a fourth-and-29 situation. The extended drive ultimately ended without a touchdown, but the penalty gave Tennessee additional life.

Simmons acknowledged the mistake after the game and apologized for the celebration.

"I also do want to say I apologize for the celebration," he said. "I was definitely in that mode, feeling myself. But, you know, it happens. Charge it to the game."

Texas head coach Steve Sarkisian described the celebration as a "bad football play" and was unhappy with the penalty. The Longhorns were charged with 11 total penalties for 115 yards during the game.

Simmons was removed from the contest following the incident before returning to the field. He responded with two consecutive sacks in the third quarter and did not celebrate either play.

fullText:
Western Michigan is not a program that receives much attention during the average college football season. That all changed in Week 1 this season when the team suffered a controversial, last-second loss to Michigan. The last second itself was the root of the controversy.

The NCAA admitted officials made the wrong call, but the result was not going to be overturned. Yet that didn't stop some AP Poll voters from acknowledging WMU after the result.

The Broncos had a golden opportunity Saturday against Boise State to pick up a win against arguably the best fellow G6 opponent and get into the driver's seat for a potential College Football Playoff berth.

The end result, however, was not what anyone in Kalamazoo had in mind. Boise State took home the 32-7 win in a game that was one-sided throughout.

The College Football Playoff features one spot reserved for the highest-ranked "Group of 6" team. That means any team not in the SEC, Big Ten, ACC, or Big 12. Notre Dame also has its own set of rules to qualify.

This leaves schools such as WMU and Boise State competing for that one spot. The two teams entered the week unranked, but did receive some votes in the AP Top 25 rankings. Other G6 teams receiving votes included Tulsa, North Dakota State, and James Madison.

This game essentially served as an early playoff game against two top G6 contenders. Boise State's blowout win officially bumps the team up into the top G6 spot, while Western Michigan will now try to win out, win the MAC, and hope for chaos.

Western Michigan fans may never let the loss to Michigan go, and rightfully so. That would have been a program-defining win, and some still consider it one even if the NCAA won't change the final result.

The loss does not technically eliminate WMU, but does make the road that much harder. At this point they would have to win out and win the MAC as a starting point. They would then need to hope teams like Boise State, Tulsa, North Dakota State, and James Madison, among others, suffer several ugly losses the rest of the way.

That seems like a lot to ask, especially with the way WMU looked Saturday. The focus may now shift to Michigan and how this impacts the team's CFP resume moving forward.

title: How GM Les Snead's philosophy has benefitted the Rams
description: The Los Angeles Rams remain Super Bowl contenders after a 1-1 start to the season because of their star-studded roster and potential.
fullText:
The Los Angeles Rams remain Super Bowl contenders after a 1-1 start to the season because of their star-studded roster and potential.

General manager Les Snead has become known for his "(Expletive) them picks" statement and philosophy over the years. In recent years, the strategy has been to package and send away draft picks for proven talent.

The philosophy led to the acquisition of veteran players such as Matthew Stafford, Jalen Ramsey and Von Miller in exchange for high draft picks. The Jacksonville Jaguars traded Ramsey to the Rams during the 2019 season, while Los Angeles acquired Stafford and Miller in 2021.

The Rams reached the Super Bowl during the 2018 and 2021 seasons, winning the latter game against the Cincinnati Bengals, 23-20, at SoFi Stadium.

Stafford remains the veteran leader for the Rams as the organization faces a familiar opportunity with the Super Bowl back in Los Angeles again this season.

Snead made two more trades, adding cornerback Trent McDuffie and edge rusher Myles Garrett during the offseason.

The Cleveland Browns sent Garrett to Los Angeles in exchange for outside linebacker Jared Verse and a 2027 first-round pick, a 2028 second-round pick, and a 2029 third-round pick.

The Kansas City Chiefs sent McDuffie to the Rams for four draft picks, including a 2026 first-round pick.

Since 2017, the Rams have only made a first-round selection twice, selecting Verse with the 19th overall pick in the 2024 NFL Draft and quarterback Ty Simpson with the 13th overall pick in 2026.

The Rams drafted quarterback Jared Goff with the No. 1 overall pick in 2016. He was sent to the Detroit Lions in exchange for Stafford.

title: Harrison Returns to Form in Brewers 102nd Win of the Year
description: The Milwaukee Brewers bullpen dominated the St. Louis Cardinals with six hitless innings.
fullText:
The Milwaukee Brewers may have just witnessed the resurgence of Kyle Harrison.

Manager Pat Murphy didn't ask too much of him, but it seems like a possible two-headed monster combination of Dustin May and Harrison could be used in the playoffs.

That won't necessarily be necessary in the best-of-five National League Division Series, but come the best-of-seven series, it sure would be nice to have those two ready to go.

Harrison improved to 11-5 on the year as he pitched two perfect innings. In fact, the only three hits the Brewers allowed in this game came off May.

May allowed two earned runs on three hits in his three innings of work. From there, the bullpen (Harrison included) combined for six innings of no-hit baseball.

As a team, the Brewers struck out 15 batters en route to a 3-2 victory over the St. Louis Cardinals. Not only did they strike out 15 batters, but May issued the lone walk of the game.

May allowed a two-out home run in the third inning, marking the second consecutive inning where he allowed a run.

The Brewers may have trailed 2-0, but they would score in the bottom of the third and later add two runs in the bottom of the fifth.

JoJo Romero picked up his 23rd hold of the season while Antonio Senzatela picked up hold No. 11.

Senzatela was only asked to record one out, but he still earned a hold in the process.

Aaron Ashby pitched the final two innings of the game and, in doing so, was able to earn his fourth save of the season.

Officially, Harrison gets the win due to May only pitching the first three innings. It's the first win for Harrison since Tuesday, Aug. 18.

Leadoff hitter Jackson Chourio went 2-for-4 with an RBI and a run while Brice Turang followed him in the lineup with a 1-for-3 night.

Turang's lone hit was his 21st home run of the season, a two-on, two-out blast off Quinn Matthews in the fifth inning.

Matthews took the loss, falling to 2-4 on the year in a game that was relatively meaningless to both teams.

If anything, it just proved how historic of a season this is for the Brewers as they're now 102-59, a record that would've been unthinkable in decades prior.

title: Desman Stephens' hit on Dante Moore was ugly. His reaction drew even more criticism

title: Ole Miss coach Pete Golding doesn't want his players 'to get this taste out of their mouth'
description: Mississippi coach Pete Golding is glad his team doesn’t play again for two weeks.  The fourth-ranked Rebels, coming off an emotional win against LSU and former Ole Miss coach Lane Kiffin, fell behind early and essentially got run off the field in a 52-28 loss to 21st-ranked Florida on Saturday. fullText:
GAINESVILLE, Fla. (AP) — Mississippi coach Pete Golding is glad his team doesn't play again for two weeks.

It gives his players extra time to stew over their failures.

The fourth-ranked Rebels, coming off an emotional win against LSU and former Ole Miss coach Lane Kiffin, fell behind early and essentially got run off the field in a 52-28 loss to 21st-ranked Florida on Saturday.

It was a huge letdown that left Golding searching for answers.

"I don't want them to get this taste out of their mouth. That's what I told them," said Golding, whose team lost to Miami in the College Football Playoff last season. "I never got the taste out of my mouth from Miami walking off the field. Part of the problem sometimes is we move on too fast."

Florida gashed Ole Miss early and often, finishing with 302 yards rushing and six touchdowns on the ground. Jadan Baugh ran for 142 yards and three scores, and backup Duke Clark added 126 yards and a score.

It was the fourth consecutive game in which the Rebels allowed at least 140 yards rushing.

"You better have that burning in your gut in order to go fix something," Golding said. "I think we have guys like that. We don't have enough guys like that right now. And that was kind of the challenge right there. We get to choose.

"That's the beautiful thing about this game. You get to choose whether you're going to go all in and do things right or not."

Golding challenged his defense during halftime — to no avail. Florida scored touchdowns on five consecutive drives in the second half.

"I think some guys took it, and other guys didn't, and I think that showed in the second half," senior linebacker Keaton Thomas said. "I'm going to make it evident, too, to call guys out and let them know that if you don't want this, then you shouldn't have come here."

Ole Miss trailed 10-0 before Heisman Trophy frontrunner Trinidad Chambliss even attempted a pass. Florida scored on the opening possession and then stopped JT Lindsey on a fourth-and-1 from their 35-yard line. Florida kicked a field goal.

The Rebels responded and scored 11 points over a three-minute stretch spanning the second and third quarters. But it was all Florida from there, with the Gators scoring touchdowns on five consecutive possessions.

"That was an old-fashioned butt-whupping," Golding said.

It didn't help that Chambliss injured his left thigh on the second drive and spent time between possessions on the exercise bike to stay loose. He completed 25 of 34 passes for 298 yards, with a touchdown, an interception and a fumble. He also ran seven times for a team-high 44 yards and two scores.

"I feel like if we were playing our best ball things might have been different, but that didn't happen today," Chambliss said.

Golding made it clear to his guys that the loss "does not define your season."

"The sun is going to come up tomorrow and we are going into a bye week, and we really have to evaluate," he said. "The things we are doing well we have to continue to do well, and we have a lot of issues in all three phases we have to address starting with coaching and playing in order to put a better product on tape because that was a butt-whupping."

A lopsided loss that included an especially egregious defensive showing.

"I addressed kind of the manhood at halftime a little bit. There was a lack of courage, in my opinion, at times, that we were picking and choosing," Golding said. "That's an elite back and he's a big back, and you've got to go chest-to-chest with him whether you like it or not.

"He's going to stiff-arm (and) you're going to be on the ground. His missed tackle rate was No. 1 in the NCAA. We watched every one of them. … But that was a big emphasis this week that obviously we did a poor job coaching because we couldn't get that done."

title: Week 3 Fantasy Football Start 'Em, Sit 'Em: Rashod Bateman vs. Jalen Coker
description: Going over who to start in fantasy football between Ravens WR Rashod Bateman and Panthers WR Jalen Coker.
fullText:
There is a group of WRs with high ceilings going into Week 3 of fantasy football, and two of those players are WRs for the Baltimore Ravens, Rashod Bateman, and WR for the Carolina Panthers, Jalen Coker. With that, here is a breakdown of which WR fantasy managers should put in their starting lineup this week between the two.

Coker through two weeks has been one of the biggest breakouts in fantasy, based on where his ADP was coming into the 2026 season. He currently has 16 receptions for 204 yards and two TDs, helping him be WR5 currently in fantasy in PPR formats. In Week 3, he and the Panthers will take on the Cleveland Browns.

The Browns have had a high and low outing regarding their passing defense's performance in two games. Against the Jacksonville Jaguars in Week 1, they allowed WR Parker Washington to record five receptions for 83 yards and a TD, in a 34-10 win. He could have had a much bigger performance if the game was closer. The Jaguars only attempted five passes in the second half. Against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in Week 2, they held their WR1, Emeka Egbuka, to three receptions for 16 yards and a TD.

In 2025, Cleveland allowed the fourth-fewest PPR fantasy points to WRs.

Bateman stepped up in a big way for the Ravens in Week 2 with their WR1 Zay Flowers out with an injury. He recorded seven receptions on nine targets for 88 yards and a TD. For the week in fantasy in PPR formats, he was WR9. Baltimore may need a similar outing in Week 3 against the Dallas Cowboys, with Flowers' snap count uncertain.

The Cowboys' passing defense looks to be somewhat improved from a season ago. In 2025, they were allowing the most passing yards per game in the NFL, 251.5. Through two games in 2026, they are allowing the 18th fewest. They have also done a solid job at defending the opposing team's WR1. New York Giants WR1 in Week 1, Malik Nabers, had six receptions for 69 yards against them. In Week 2, Washington Commanders WR1 Terry McLaurin had two receptions for 50 yards.

When it comes to who should start and who should sit between Bateman and Coker in Week 3 in fantasy football, Coker should start, and Bateman should sit.

Coker has been too good thus far in 2026 to warrant sitting him out. His fantasy floor feels higher than Bateman's for Week 3 with the volume he has received early on this season. He has 18 targets, which is tied for the most on the team with Carolina WR1 Tetairoa McMillan.

Bateman is still a good starting option, but banking on him having a better fantasy outing than Coker, coming off a 2025 season where he did not have a single game with over 70 receiving yards, is just too big an ask. Especially if Flowers plays any sort of role in the game.

title: Guardians clinch third consecutive AL Central crown, No. 2 seed
description: The Guardians clinched after beating the Royals 11-5, and after the White Sox lost to the Rockies 9-6.
fullText:
The Cleveland Guardians had already clinched a playoff berth, but now have also secured the AL Central crown.

The Guardians' 11-5 victory over the Kansas City Royals helped Cleveland lock in the No. 2 seed in the American League playoff bracket and cement their place atop the AL Central. Cleveland has won the AL Central three years in a row, and four of the last five years.

For the third consecutive year, the American League Central runs through Cleveland.#GuardsBall | #StandGuard pic.twitter.com/NFjtRYWpQM

Cleveland clinched with the help of the Colorado Rockies. After their win, the Guardians needed the Chicago White Sox to lose, and the Rockies delivered with a 9-6 victory. Afterward, Colorado acknowledged what it helped Cleveland achieve and made sure the Guardians knew as well, in a hilarious way, on social media.

ROCKIES WIN!@CleGuardians you can address your thank yous to:

2001 Blake Street
Denver, CO 80205 pic.twitter.com/95tIYTZZ3v

The Guardians move to 85-76 on the season with the win. They are the second-best division winner in the AL, and the No. 1 seed in the league has already been secured by the Tampa Bay Rays (97-63). With only one day of games left on Sunday, the eventual AL West winner cannot surpass Cleveland's win total, locking the Guardians into the No. 2 seed.

Cleveland will take on the Boston Red Sox in the AL Wild Card Series. Boston will be the No. 5 seed, the third AL East team to make the playoffs. The Guardians and Red Sox played six games against each other during the regular season and tied, taking three games apiece.

There is only one American League playoff spot still up for grabs. The quest for the AL West crown is coming down to the wire between the Texas Rangers and the Houston Astros. Whichever team wins the division will be the No. 3 seed, and will face the No. 4 seed New York Yankees in the Wild Card round.

Cleveland did not make it out of the Wild Card round last season. The Guardians were matched up with the Detroit Tigers and lost the three-game series 2-1.

Steven Vogt has been Cleveland's manager since 2024. Since taking over the team, he has led them to a 265-219 record with three playoff berths.

The Guardians haven't been to the World Series since 2016. That was the year that the Chicago Cubs finally broke their curse by winning the World Series, defeating the Guardians 4-3 in the 7-game series.

As part of their frustrating 41-31 loss to the Buffalo Bills at Highmark Stadium last Thursday, multiple Detroit Lions players were slapped with fines from the NFL for various infractions.

Hit particularly hard by the NFL in the wallet was wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown, who was issued four separate citations, totaling nearly $60,000 worth of fines. He wasn't the only one who has to write a check, as teammates Jameson Williams, Penei Sewell and Jahmyr Gibbs were all hit with fines as well.

However, the star Lions wideout plans on issuing an appeal.

St. Brown was hit with four separate penalties by the NFL on unsportsmanlike conduct; the total amount he's now required to pony up to the League is just over $59,000.

However, as St. Brown explained, he plans on appealing the decision.

"It's not good, man. 14 something times four, you do the math," St. Brown said Thursday via Nolan Dianchi of the Detroit News. "But I'm gonna appeal it."

"Players subject to accountability measures receive a letter informing them of what they did, a video of the play in question, why they are being fined and how much it will cost them," the league writes in the rulebook. "They also receive information on how to appeal the fine. If they choose not to appeal, the fine is withheld from their next game check."

fullText:
The Denver Broncos made their final roster moves with Adam Prentice and Mitchell Fraboni as they are currently set up. However, the Broncos also added Kolbe Katsis to their game-day roster, which is good news for him, but creates questions for the group.

"#Broncos have promoted LS Mitch Fraboni to the 53-man roster, per the wire," the Denver Post's Parker Gabriel reported on X on September 26, anddding that they were also "Elevating FB Adam Prentice (third and final time) and undrafted WR Kolbe Katsis from the practice squad for Sunday night.

We've made a series of roster moves.

Notably, the rules that now restrict Prentice from being elevated a third time also apply to Fraboni, who would need to be signed to the Broncos' 53-man roster to be their long snapper in Week 4 against the San Francisco 49ers.

Fraboni is the Broncos' only long snapper, so a move to the 53-man roster seems likely.

The Broncos have tight end Nate Adkins, who also serves as an H-back. Still, Prentice has been a staple for the Broncos and head coach Sean Payton for years.

fullText:
Well, in their quest to aid major-league history and prevent a sub-.500 team from winning their division, the Texas Rangers knocked the Twins around in a rain-delayed, 6-2 victory on Saturday afternoon. With the Houston Astros just underway, the Rangers improve to 80-81, and give themselves a fighting chance of claiming the West with another win tomorrow afternoon; if they do, they will at least guarantee that their ticket to the playoffs will come on the back of an even record.

For the first time since 2009, the Rangers hit four doubles in the same inning, a four-run second that summed up most of Bailey Ober's day. Nicky Lopez, Evan Carter, Alejandro Osuna, and Brandon Nimmo each had a two-bagger in the inning, which saw Ober give up four of his six earned runs, and five of his ten hits — all with two outs in the inning and nobody aboard.

It closed the book on Ober for 2026, leaving him with a 7-7 record and 4.47 ERA. He added five strikeouts and one walk to his final marks.

The Twins were not as successful in getting to Texas starter Nathan Eovaldi, who did not make it through five frames after tossing 71 pitches and booking it. Luke Keaschall doubled and scored in the first, but only three other Twins would tag Eovaldi for a hit, and the only other Twins run came after the white-hot Keaschall tripled and scored on a Josh Bell single in the bottom of the eighth.

The book is nearly closed on all the members of the Twins roster, with Dean Kremer scheduled to start Game 162 and finish off this season for good. Minnesota currently sits at 76-85, dead even with the Detroit Tigers; a win and a Tiger loss tomorrow would leave the Twins alone in third place to end the season.

title: Wolverines vow to 'come together' after deflating walk-off loss
description: Michigan endured its first loss of the season, on the last play to Iowa, and now it’s about how the Wolverines will rebound.
fullText:
ANN ARBOR — Michigan endured its first loss of the season, on the last play to Iowa, and now it's about how the Wolverines will rebound.

After losing to the Hawkeyes, 20-19, on a 16-yard touchdown pass with no time left on Saturday, Sept. 26, Michigan (3-1, 0-1 Big Ten) goes on the road for the first time this season and will face Minnesota next weekend.

"We're gonna come together," defensive lineman Enow Etta said. "We got how many games ahead of us? It happened. We just gotta build on it. How do we let something like this not happen again? So we just gotta hit it Sunday, Monday, the rest of the week and work on 1-0 next week."

Offensive tackle Evan Link said the team is looking forward to getting back on the field against the Golden Gophers.

"It's another chance to go out there and get better as a team and continue to work on the things you want to work on," Link said.

While a road game can galvanize a team, Etta said home or away, this team just needs to be better.

"We got to punch people in the mouth and execute home or away," Etta said. "It's less about the game and more about us. How are we gonna respond to this? Home or away, we gotta respond. We gotta work this week harder than we ever have because what we did last week wasn't good enough. We just gotta put our head down and execute."

Michigan was without starting right tackle Andrew Sprague for a second straight game, and offensive lineman Manuel Beigel, who has been used as an extra lineman at the "rhino" spot, also was not available.

Sprague was a late scratch before Game 3 against UTEP for an undisclosed reason. He was on the sideline for the Iowa game. In his absence, Blake Frazier flipped from left tackle to right, and Link, who started the season at left guard, moved to left tackle.

Frazier went down with what looked like an injury to his right leg during Michigan's second series of the second half, but after a quick visit to the medical tent, he returned to the game.

"Blake's a really tough guy, and I think nothing would have kept him out of this game," Link said after the loss to Iowa. "Whatever happened to him, I'll find out (Sunday) and I'm sure he's going to do whatever he can to be out there next Saturday as well. Kid's a really, really tough guy, and I know he's going to do everything he can to play."

Sprague's status remains unclear. Coach Kyle Whittingham said Monday night on the "Inside Michigan Football" radio show that Sprague could be out anywhere from this week to several weeks. Right guard Brady Norton suggested, during an interview with reporters Tuesday after practice, that it was Sprague's decision to pull himself from the lineup before the UTEP game.

"I'd rather let him be safe and healthy throughout the rest of the season than have him force himself to play against UTEP and get hurt and be out for the rest of the season," Norton said. "So I'm glad he made the decision he did, and I want him to be patient and make sure he comes back as healthy as he can so he can get back in the lineup."

Michigan did not force a turnover against Iowa but did give up an interception. The Wolverines are now minus-four in turnover margin this season.

"Coaches has been preaching to us, and we've been preaching to each other, we got to get the ball — punchouts, turnovers, interception, whatever," Enow said. "We got to score on defense like we have sometimes the last few years. We just got to continue to emphasize on that. Whatever we got to do, we got to do it better. We need to we get the ball back to the offense in critical situations and put them in good position."

Michigan's defense did such a solid job keeping Iowa from scoring offensively in the first half, but the Hawkeyes tied the game at 7 on Braeden Jackson's 99-yard kickoff return in the first quarter.

"That was huge," Whittingham said. "We got to coach it better. We weren't trying to kick it to him. We were trying to kick it out of the back of the end zone, and he took it back on us."

Whittingham on the loss: "It's a shame we let that one get away from us, because we had it."
